summary.headline: Indoco Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 25.8% YoY to INR 4,291 mn and EBITDA margin hit 14.7%, with international formulations up 94.6%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the first positive quarter in about six quarters, driven by international formulations in regulated and emerging markets, while India was muted by a weak season in anti-infectives and respiratory. Standalone EBITDA rose to INR 630 mn (14.7%) from INR 35 mn a year earlier. Trade receivables rose sharply, mainly on long-credit emerging-market collections, and supplier/MSME payables were stretched. Consolidated debt is about INR 960 crore, with management guiding to roughly INR 140 crore of annual repayments and a tight capex freeze. Management also announced the hive-off of its India and Africa ophthalmic business to Sunway.

segments.name: Regulated markets
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,401 mn, +78.3% YoY. US INR 546 mn (+77.5%), Europe INR 786 mn (+68.7%), South Africa/Australia/NZ INR 692 mn (from INR 122 mn on a small base).

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 746 mn, +134% YoY (from INR 318 mn). Management cited longer receivable periods in this segment.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 315 mn, down 23% YoY (from INR 409 mn). Warren Remedies API capex is not yet generating sales as products await validation and approvals.

segments.name: Services (AnaCipher CRO and Indoco Analytical Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 895 mn, +65.3% YoY (from INR 467 mn).

segments.name: Domestic formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,739 mn vs INR 1,851 mn a year ago. Anti-infectives and respiratory were hit; management said stockist and primary sales fell while prescriptions grew. Stomatology primary sales were down 20% against IQVIA down 8%.

segments.name: Franchise/OTC (Warren Remedies)
segments.commentary: FY26 OTC revenue about INR 120 crore; Q4 OTC revenue INR 27.4 crore. Warren is loss-making, with Q4 consolidated FPP plus Warren net worth negative.

guidance_outlook: Debt repayments of about INR 140 crore a year for FY27, FY28 and FY29, with a target to prepay slightly more.
Average cost of borrowing about 8.5-9%; management implied interest savings of roughly INR 120 crore from the repayment schedule.
No major capex planned over the next two years; capex is under tight control and opex reduction is underway.
Europe margins expected to improve in the coming year as contract manufacturing moves to plants that have completed MMP scale-ups.
Management expects Warren Remedies API turnaround in a couple of quarters, with a regulated-market approval for the API site taking about one more year.
Management expects India business to grow in line with IPM and expects FPP product-mix COGS hits to reduce.
capex_capacity: Warren Remedies toothpaste block: only 1 of 4 planned lines installed; the second line (mouthwash) is deferred. First toothpaste export to South Africa started at about INR 37 lakh.
Patalganga API site: validations in progress; management is trying to speed USFDA approval by shifting a product's site from Patalganga to another site.
Sterile US supply is constrained at the existing plant pending FDA approvals; second sites now bill some sterile sales.
Liquid orals ANDA approvals received in the US for Brivaracetam and Lacosamide; launches planned in the US and Europe in FY27.
demand_pricing: Prescriptions (Rx) are growing across almost all main brands, but primary sales fell in Q4 as field staff missed annual targets; the company expects primary to correct as IQVIA follows Rx.
Cital (urinary alkalizer) was down 10% YoY and 1% QoQ in Q4 on a weak summer, though IQVIA is growing and channel stock is under 30 days.

Management said Rexidin-M Forte gel became the most prescribed stomatological brand (January and March on a max basis). Indoco overtook Pfizer to become the 20th most prescribed company by prescriptions.
Europe and UK pricing is volatile; the company is holding back on small molecules where margins are inadequate, including some Clarity Pharma products.
Emerging-market focus is Eastern Africa (Kenya, Tanzania, Zambia) and about 8 French West African countries.
The FPP Q4 COGS spike came from low-margin trading products, expired-product write-offs of about INR 4 crore, and shelf-stock adjustments.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables (up 45% vs revenue up about 9%) and rising debt and MSME payables.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the receivables rise to long-credit emerging-market collections, with regulated-market exports up about 28-29%. Debt is about INR 960 crore, flat vs last year. Some supplier payments were late due to cash-flow strain, and management expects to settle within a week.

qa_highlights.question: Why Rx growth has not translated into sales, and whether the India business will recover.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 primary shortfall reflects weak field motivation and seasonality, with stockists holding low inventory. It expects IQVIA and primary sales to follow Rx and said India should grow in line with IPM.

qa_highlights.question: Why FPP's net worth turned more negative in Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the swing to low-margin trading sales, a COGS spike, and expired-product write-offs of about INR 4 crore. Management noted that the net worth figure includes Warren Remedies, which is also loss-making.

qa_highlights.question: Exchange loss and the interest cost increase.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the exchange loss on the EUR 10 mn ECB loan at Oral Remedies was about INR 24 mn, roughly half of the quarter's finance cost.

qa_highlights.question: The INR 23 crore held-for-sale asset and the provision for doubtful debts.
qa_highlights.answer: The held-for-sale asset is a land parcel carried at book value, which management expects to sell above book. The roughly INR 10 crore provision includes a bankrupt customer and a policy-based provision on old disputed receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Debt repayment schedule and interest-cost savings.
qa_highlights.answer: Repayments are about INR 140 crore a year for FY27-FY29. Management cited an average borrowing cost of about 8.5-9%, implying roughly INR 120 crore of lower interest cost.

qa_highlights.question: Europe and US growth drivers and FDA-related constraints.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe margins should improve as MMP scale-ups complete, with only a small paracetamol residual left. US growth is driven by solid orals, while sterile supply awaits FDA approvals.

risks_watch: Receivables days and emerging-market collections, given rising trade receivables and MSME payable stretch.
Debt: about INR 960 crore consolidated, with about INR 344 crore short-term; delivery on the INR 140 crore repayment schedule.
US sterile approvals at the existing plant, and the timing of FDA approval for Warren/API sites.
Ophthalmic business hive-off to Sunway (India and Africa): deal completion and revenue impact.
Warren Remedies losses and advertising spend (about 3 years' support committed); API site validations.
Seasonality in India: Cital and anti-infective recovery, and stockist restocking.
Rivaroxaban US share (only one strength approved) and apixaban launch timing.
Currency exposure from the EUR ECB loan and the impact of the war on the exchange rate.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Rx growth, international momentum and debt servicing, but defensive on receivables, payables and the Warren/API losses. Several answers were vague on timelines (FDA, apixaban, Clarity), and some figures needed correction during the call.

So, what is that is the primary reason of receivables, which are number of days of receivables, which are going up.
Yes, there has been some, where we have not paid suppliers on time given some of the cash flow situation we had.
So, next financial year which is '26-'27 we have a commitment to repay 140.
